sentences.text:
This bail application under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the
applicant- Shailendra Kumar, seeking enlargement on bail during trial in connection with Case
Crime No. 366 of 2023, under Sections 182, 195, 211, 386, 420, 376, 120-B I.P.C., registered at
Police Station Tundala, District Firozabad.

3.  The first information report of the present case was lodged on 16.05.2023 by the applicant against Shiv Kumar Verma alleging therein that his younger sister-in-law aged about 17 years was living with him since last 12 days.
On 16.05.2023 Shiv Kumar Verma took her to Vaishno Devi Temple and then took her to J.P. Hotel where he committed rape on her.

Her sister-in-law told him about the Shailendra Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54062764/
1 incident on phone on which he informed the police.

sentences.text: On this information he reached the hotel where the police also reached and the victim told him about the incident.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the applicant is the first informant himself.

It is argued that the first information report in the matter was initially lodged under sections 376 I.P.C.
and section 3 (2) (v) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities Act),
1989.

entities.text:
Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities Act),
1989
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The victim in her statement recorded u/s 161 Cr.P.C. has given a detailed version as to how in an effort to get Government employment she herself entangled the accused Shiv Kumar Verma on the saying of Bantu, Swami and Shailendra (the applicant).

It is further argued that the victim in her statement recorded u/s 164 Cr.P.C. improves the version and gives an improved version of the incident wherein she names Shiv Shankar as the accused and states of Bantu, Sonu and Shailendra lured her to entangle Shiv Kumar Verma.
It is argued that the police without any credible evidence has implicated the applicant in the present matter.
It is further argued that the victim in her statement recorded u/s 161 Cr.P.C. and also in her statement recorded u/s 164 Cr.P.C. has disclosed her age as 22 years.

It is argued that during investigation the matter was converted from a case under sections 376 I.P.C. and section 3 (2) (v) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities Act), 1989 to sections 182, 195, 211, 386, 420, 376, 120-B I.P.C.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities Act), 1989
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The applicant has no criminal history as stated in para 20 of the affidavit and is in jail since 27.05.2023.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer for bail.
6. After having heard the learned counsel for the parties and perusing the record, it is evident that that the applicant is the first informant of the matter.

The case was converted from the case under sections 376 I.P.C. and section 3 (2) (v) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities Act), 1989 to sections 182, 195, 211, 386, 420, 376, 120-B I.P.C.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities Act), 1989
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The applicant has been made as an accused in the matter.

There was a plot by the applicant and his two associates along with the victim to somehow get Government employment to the victim through Shiv Kumar Verma for which the victim had lured him and entangled him.

7. Looking to the facts and circumstances of this case, the nature of evidence and also the absence of any convincing material to indicate the possibility of tampering with the evidence, this Court is of the view that the applicant may be enlarged on bail.

8. Let the applicant- Shailendra Kumar, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties (one of the sureties will be of family members and the other will be of a local person) each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
i) The applicant will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not harm or harass the victim/complainant in any manner whatsoever.
ii) The applicant will abide the orders of court, will attend the court on every date and will not delay the disposal of trial in any manner whatsoever.

sentences.text: (iii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the date fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(iv) The applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail in any manner whatsoever.

In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under section 174-A I.P.C.
(v) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law and the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A IPC.
(vi) The trial court may make all possible efforts/endeavour and try to conclude the trial expeditiously after the release of the applicant.

9. The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned and in case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail and send the applicant to prison.
10. The bail application is allowed.
